title: Relative m-pseudo-coherence descends along fppf scheme coverings
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $f:X\to B$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions], let $m\in\mathbf Z$, and let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] have quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $J$ be a set and let $\{p_j:X_j\to X\}_{j\in J}$ be an fppf covering of schemes [def-pc-fppf-site], meaning that every $p_j$ is flat and locally of finite presentation and their images jointly cover $X$. Each $X_j$ is viewed over $B$ by $f\circ p_j$. Then $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $B$ [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex] if and only if $Lp_j^*E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $B$ for every $j\in J$ [def-pc-derived-pullback]. There is no Noetherian, quasi-compactness, separation, or global cohomological boundedness hypothesis.

proof.text: Assume $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $B$. Each $p_j$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, so $\mathcal O_{X_j}[0]$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $X$ by the flat-lfp structure lemma. Local finite presentation implies local finite type directly from the affine finite-presentation definition, and local finite type is closed under composition. Apply the relative pullback lemma to $X_j\to X\to B$, for this same $m$, to obtain the forward implication.

We first prepare the converse for a surjective finite locally free $\pi:Y\to Z$, where $Z\to B$ is locally of finite type. By the definition of finite locally free morphisms, $\pi$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, so its algebra $A=\pi_*\mathcal O_Y$ is finite locally free. Locally trivialize it near $z\in Z$, and write the section $1$ as $(a_1,\ldots,a_d)$. Affine pushforward base change identifies $A\otimes\kappa(z)$, as a unital algebra, with the coordinate ring of the fibre. The image of $1$ is nonzero: the fibre of the surjective map $\pi$ is a nonempty affine scheme, hence its coordinate ring has $1\ne0$. Thus some $a_i$ is a unit in $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$. Shrink so it is invertible and define $r:A\to\mathcal O_Z$ by $r(b_1,\ldots,b_d)=a_i^{-1}b_i$. Then $r(1)=1$, and the explicit maps $b\mapsto(r(b),b-r(b)1)$ and $(c,q)\mapsto c1+q$ identify $A$ with $\mathcal O_Z\oplus\ker r$. This argument uses no division by the rank; it also applies in residue characteristic dividing $d$.

Let $F\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ and assume $L\pi^*F$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $B$. Derived pullback preserves quasi-coherent cohomology. Hence the finite-pushforward lemma makes $R\pi_*L\pi^*F$ $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $B$. The source $Y\to B$ is locally of finite type by composition. The map $\pi$ is finite, hence proper, thus quasi-compact and separated by definition and quasi-separated by the separatedness lemma. It is affine by the definition of finite. Apply the projection formula with $\mathcal O_Y[0]$ and $F$. For this affine map, termwise pushforward of a K-injective resolution of the quasi-coherent complex $\mathcal O_Y[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism from $\pi_*\mathcal O_Y[0]=A[0]$ by the affine resolution comparison, so $R\pi_*\mathcal O_Y\cong A[0]$ by the definition of derived direct image. With the unit isomorphism $\mathcal O_Y\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\pi^*F\cong L\pi^*F$ and the symmetry of the derived tensor structure, the formula gives an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_Z)$:
$$R\pi_*L\pi^*F\cong F\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_Z} A[0].$$

On each neighbourhood of step 2, the displayed splitting of $A$ induces
$$F\otimes^{\mathbf L}A[0]\cong F\oplus(F\otimes^{\mathbf L}(\ker r)[0]).$$
Indeed tensor a K-flat representative of $F$ with the two inverse module maps of step 2: additivity of the total tensor gives the two inverse complex maps, and localization gives this isomorphism. By step 3, $F\otimes^{\mathbf L}A[0]$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $B$ on $Z$; by the all-affine-charts criterion (every affine chart of the open neighbourhood is a chart of $Z$, and such charts exist), its restriction to each neighbourhood is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $B$. Relative $m$-pseudo-coherence is invariant under isomorphism by its definition, so the relative direct-summand lemma gives it for $F$ on these neighbourhoods. Source locality glues them. We have therefore proved descent along each surjective finite locally free map, keeping the fixed $m$.

Now assume every $Lp_j^*E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $B$. Apply the fppf refinement lemma to the scheme $X$ and the covering $\{X_j\to X\}$. It supplies opens $X=\bigcup_a U_a$, surjective finite locally free $W_a\to U_a$, opens $W_a=\bigcup_b W_{ab}$, surjective finite locally free $T_{ab}\to W_{ab}$, indices $j(a,b)$, and $X$-morphisms $\alpha_{ab}:T_{ab}\to X_{j(a,b)}$. Write $q_{ab}:T_{ab}\to X$ for the whole composite; then $p_{j(a,b)}\alpha_{ab}=q_{ab}$. The refinement is on $X$, not on $B$.

Each $q_{ab}$ is flat and locally of finite presentation: its factors are open immersions or finite locally free maps. For flatness, on local rings use composition of flat maps; for local finite presentation use its composition lemma. The open-immersion factors are localizations and thus flat and locally of finite presentation. Hence $\mathcal O_{T_{ab}}[0]$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $X$, as is $\mathcal O_{X_{j(a,b)}}[0]$. The maps to $X$ are locally of finite type, and $\alpha_{ab}$ is locally of finite type by cancellation from $p_{j(a,b)}\alpha_{ab}=q_{ab}$. Apply relative-composition invariance to $T_{ab}\xrightarrow{\alpha_{ab}}X_{j(a,b)}\to X$, with the object $\mathcal O_{T_{ab}}[0]$, for every integer degree. It is therefore pseudo-coherent relative to $X_{j(a,b)}$. No flatness of $\alpha_{ab}$ is needed.

Apply relative pullback to $\alpha_{ab}$ and $Lp_{j(a,b)}^*E$. All three morphisms in $T_{ab}\to X_{j(a,b)}\to B$ are locally of finite type by step 6 and composition with $X\to B$. The result and the composition isomorphism for derived pullback give
$$Lq_{ab}^*E\cong L\alpha_{ab}^*Lp_{j(a,b)}^*E$$
$m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $B$. Every pulled-back complex that occurs in the refinement has quasi-coherent cohomology by preservation under derived pullback.

Use the finite locally free descent proved in steps 2--4 on $T_{ab}\to W_{ab}$. It gives $m$-pseudo-coherence relative to $B$ for the pullback of $E$ to each $W_{ab}$. Source locality glues this on $W_a$. Use steps 2--4 again on $W_a\to U_a$, and source locality again on $X=\bigcup_a U_a$. The result is $m$-pseudo-coherence of $E$ relative to $B$. All intermediate structure maps to $B$ are locally of finite type, and all intermediate objects have quasi-coherent cohomology, as checked above. If $X$ is empty, the definition is vacuous and the same empty-cover assembly applies. No finite subcover or uniform cohomological bound is used.
